findings.note: NEW at run phoenix-nft-staking-13. Distinct root cause from H-01 (mempool race vs. value-blind gate). Report generated and PoC (poc-MevFrontrunNudge.t.sol) validated passing; moved to submitted. [TRIAGE 2026-05-29] Accepted — valid finding. Mitigation: introduce a `minRewardPayout` parameter so the claimer can use AMM-style slippage mechanics to revert the transaction if their expected reward has been front-run/claimed. This protects an honest batch-minter from spending a large sum and receiving nothing. [TRIAGE 2026-05-30] ACCEPTED as residual (user triage 2026-05-30). Threat model verified against batchMint @ 9be4a87: (cond.2) claiming the nudge requires paying nudgeSize×mintPrice for real mints — the owner-pinned minter/dispatcher (story-009) make a free claim impossible (verified L257-259, L270); (cond.1) the minReward floor (L278-279) reverts the loser's batch atomically so a sniped user never overpays for a gone reward. Winner-take-all MEV capture remains by design and is accepted: nudge reward is a fraction of NFT mint cost, NFTs have no secondary market (only the staking pool), so a pure MEV bot cannot recoup in one tx — a front-runner who claims must genuinely join the protocol, reducing the issue to an ordinary gas auction among real participants. ACCEPTANCE INVARIANT (owner-operational, not code-enforced): keep the nudge pot < nudgeSize×mintPrice; if the yield funnel ever lets the pot exceed the cost of nudgeSize mints, pure-profit MEV returns. Also assumes a non-zero dispatcher mint price when the nudge is funded. [phoenix-nft-staking-16 RE-TRIAGE] The acceptance invariant 'keep pot < nudgeSize x mintPrice' does NOT bound loss if the minted NFTs carry realizable (resellable/redeemable) value: a searcher who realizes NFT value nets ~pot>0 for ANY pot size, so the giveaway is raced to zero on every refill — the 'NFTs have no secondary market' premise of the 2026-05-30 acceptance no longer holds if a market/redemption path exists (RETRIAGE-001 / ECON-002 / cross-ref F-01 lineage). Over-funding facet (PATTERN-002) is a non-obvious Law-3 owner footgun ('fund the incentive' silently == 'set a sweepable bounty'). Severity ceiling RE-CONFIRMED MEDIUM (NOT secretly High: no principal theft, honest minters still receive NFTs and story-015 minReward reverts a sniped honest caller atomically; loss bounded by owner funding; mempool ordering race, not an unconditional drain). This is fully closed by the `minReward` slippage floor (story-015): if the pot has been front-run, the batch reverts atomically and the honest user pays nothing. The remaining race — who wins the pot among qualifying batches — is an accepted gas-auction among genuine protocol participants, each of whom must pay the full mint cost. `nudgeSize` ensures no free-claim path exists (story-009). Marked fixed at HEAD 5f863d27 per owner triage 2026-06-09. [phoenix-nft-staking-20] ⚠ EXPIRED-CLOSURE — REOPEN PROPOSED at Medium (severity assessed AT HEAD, historical label given no weight). findings.label: M-07
findings.title: forceApprove(nftMinter, type(uint256).max) lets an under-funded batch silently spend the contract's own payment-token balance
findings.note: [phoenix-nft-staking-20] NEW MEDIUM @0d1a0b2. batchMint step 6 does forceApprove(nftMinter, type(uint256).max) before the mint loop, so the allowance is unbounded WITHIN the loop: a batch with count=N but payment for only M < N mints does NOT revert as the NatSpec at :69-71 and §3 steps 5/6 claim — mints M+1..N are funded from the contract's own standing balance (donations, sub-DUST_THRESHOLD dust, the nudge pot), the caller receives N NFTs, and totalPaid under-reports the true dispatcher cost. findings.label: L-06
findings.title: A staker wired to a BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook on which it is not the recipient reverts on EVERY _syncBudget path
findings.note: [phoenix-nft-staking-20] NEW LOW @0d1a0b2, severityCeiling MEDIUM (recorded, not resolved). A staker wired to a BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook on which it is not the recipient reverts on EVERY _syncBudget path: pull() is onlyOwnerOrRecipient and additionally reverts RecipientUnset when recipient == address(0), and the staker calls it with msg.sender == itself — so stake, unstake, claim, depositFor, initiateMigration and pullAndRefresh ALL revert unconditionally, even when mintDebt is zero. In a cross-staker migration the TARGET is BY CONSTRUCTION not yet the hook's recipient, so wiring the target's dispatcherHook before flipping hook.setRecipient bricks the migration at the first depositFor. Held at Low: recovery is clean and owner-side (two independent un-brick routes — flip setRecipient, or setDispatcherHook(address(0))), principal always escapes (emergencyWithdraw and userMigrate never call pull()), and no value is at risk at any point. If the operator judges a half-executed migration with custody already moved to be an availability EVENT, Medium is defensible — the ceiling is the instrument for that. Checked and REFUTED (severity-auditor): the adjacent stranding worry does NOT apply — NFTStakerMigrator.migrate is atomic (batchMigrate + every depositFor in one transaction), so a reverting depositFor rolls the ERC1155 pull back rather than stranding it in the no-rescue migrator. Recorded so nobody re-derives it. REMEDY: document the wiring ORDER as a mandatory runbook step (flip hook.setRecipient BEFORE setDispatcherHook on the target) and add an orchestrator test that wires a real recipient-guarded hook to the target. ⚠ D-15 DISCLOSURE against ledger L-02 966e717669f9… (open, src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol, un-try/catch'd dispatcherHook.pull()): same 'hook bricks every _syncBudget path' class recurring on copy #4 via a DIFFERENT trigger. findings.note: [phoenix-nft-staking-20] NEW — ⚠ ROUTED TO THE SPEC-CONFORMANCE REPORT ONLY (orchestrator ruling R-4). NOT filed in the security stream and deliberately given NO L-xx label. docs/multi-token-nudge.md §1 claims the pot is 'by construction a fraction of the cost of the nudgeSize mints' and that 'there is no configuration of this mechanism under which claiming is profitable-in-isolation'.
